display.title: Episode 162: The Forbidden Road, Chapter 2 (Tu B'Shvat)
display.summary_short: A Tu B'Shvat show: the trees wish each other a happy new year, Nanas the butcher earns a place in Gan Eden by caring for his parents, and Reb Beryl is saved through a promise of tzedakah.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on the eve of Tu B'Shvat, the New Year for Trees. Uncle Yossi pictures the trees wishing each other a happy new year and explains the custom of eating fruits of Eretz Yisroel with the brachah and Shehecheyanu. The march is the song of the second of the Twelve Pesukim, Shema Yisrael. Mitzvah Time announces an essay contest and tells how the sage Rabbi Yehoshua dreamed that his place in Gan Eden would be beside Nanas the butcher, a simple man who devotedly fed, washed and dressed his aged parents. A caller reads her essay about giving her seat on the train to an old man, and after the sponsor and the Shema with a visiting family, the story concludes. The Rebbe tells the penniless Reb Beryl that it is never too late for teshuvah and has him promise to give a tenth of all his money to tzedakah. That night the officer celebrates with wine, falls asleep, and the maid sweeps the signed paper into the fire. Reb Beryl's property is saved; he apologizes to his son's teacher, brings him back and gives tzedakah generously. The show ends with the Tu B'Shvat cover of the Moshiach Times.
display.lesson: Give tzedakah generously, for Hashem blesses those who share; and honoring parents can earn the highest place in Gan Eden.
